scenarios.title: Clean boot from reset to blink and UART
scenarios.hidden_symptom: LED blinks and the terminal shows three lines.
scenarios.expected: All six boot steps pass, "boot ok", "counter=1" and "greeting_len=7" are printed, no faults, halt at the end of main.

scenarios.title: Boot fault - startup code forgets to zero .bss
scenarios.hidden_symptom: LED blinks, 'boot ok' prints, but 'counter=' shows a huge number instead of 1 and it changes between power cycles.
scenarios.expected: Boot reaches main without faults, but the bss_zeroed step reports garbage and "counter=" is not 1.

scenarios.title: Boot fault - wrong initial stack pointer in the vector table
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Board prints 'boot ok' then hangs; the debugger shows the core in lockup with HFSR.FORCED set.
scenarios.expected: Boot steps up to main_entered pass (vector_table flagged); the first push is a BusFault escalated to HardFault, its entry fails with STKERR, and the core locks up.

scenarios.title: Interrupt latency - button IRQ with a GPIO marker, light vs heavy load
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Button response is usually instant but sometimes visibly late; the latency histogram has a long tail.
scenarios.expected: Light load gives a tight histogram near the 12-cycle entry cost; heavy load spreads it up to the critical-section length with much larger jitter.

scenarios.title: Two interrupts - priority inversion vs fixed priorities, tail-chaining
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Button response time depends on whether the timer handler happens to be running.
scenarios.expected: With equal priorities the button waits ~500 cycles and is tail-chained after the timer; with a higher priority it is taken in ~12 cycles by pre-empting the timer handler.

scenarios.title: Three-task round-robin kernel on the SysTick
scenarios.hidden_symptom: LED blinks, alphabet scrolls, counter increments; three things happen at once on one core.
scenarios.expected: 30 ticks, 40+ context switches, all tasks alive, the alphabet appears on the UART, the LED toggles, stack watermarks around 25 percent, no faults.

scenarios.title: Misbehaving task hits the MPU stack guard - kernel kills it, others continue
scenarios.hidden_symptom: One of the three tasks stops; the other two keep going; the fault log shows a MemManage with an address just below a stack.
scenarios.expected: One MemManage fault with MMARVALID pointing into guard_C; task C is DEAD with a 100 percent watermark; A and B keep running; no lockup.

scenarios.title: Context switch bug - PendSV forgets to save and restore r8
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Tasks run, but one of them occasionally computes garbage or resets its counter; nothing in the fault log.
scenarios.expected: No faults, tasks keep switching, but task A reports r8 corruptions (marker events) and the "corruptions" global is non-zero.

scenarios.title: Stack overflow without the MPU - watermark hits 100 percent, then corruption
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Random tasks crash with UsageFault or BusFault at nonsense addresses; which one crashes changes with timing.
scenarios.expected: No MemManage; instead a late BusFault/UsageFault chain, more than one task dead, C's watermark 100 percent and corrupted globals.

scenarios.title: Flash vs SRAM - the same loop timed with the cycle counter, with and without the XIP cache
scenarios.hidden_symptom: The same function runs faster when moved to RAM, but only a little, unless the cache is off.
scenarios.expected: sram is fastest, flash_cached is within a few percent of it (only cold misses), flash_uncached is several times slower; the instruction count is identical in all three.

scenarios.title: ISA comparison - the same benchmark under the arm_like and riscv_like cost profiles
scenarios.hidden_symptom: The RISC-V build is larger and retires fewer instructions for the same C code.
scenarios.expected: Both profiles execute the same program; they differ in instret (riscv_like retires fewer because it has compare-and-branch instructions, but more for push/pop), in cycles and CPI, and in static code size (arm_like denser).

scenarios.title: SVC system call path - privilege round trip, an ignored cpsid and a forbidden SysTick write
scenarios.hidden_symptom: A task that tries to disable interrupts has no effect at all; the same task dies with a BusFault when it touches SysTick.
scenarios.expected: Several svc write calls succeed with a privilege round trip each; cpsid in task C is ignored; the SysTick write is a precise BusFault (BFAR=0xE000E010); C is DEAD, A and B keep running, no lockup.

scenarios.title: Boot fault - startup code forgets to copy .data from flash
scenarios.hidden_symptom: 'boot ok' and 'counter=1' print correctly, but a configuration value that was initialised in the source reads as a random number.
scenarios.expected: Boot reaches main without faults; the data_copied step reports a mismatch; "counter=1" is correct but "greeting_len=" is not 7.

scenarios.title: HardFault at reset - the reset vector is missing the Thumb bit
scenarios.hidden_symptom: The board never prints 'boot ok'; the only output is a HardFault dump.
scenarios.expected: The vector_table step reports the missing Thumb bit; Reset_Handler never runs; a HardFault (FORCED) escalated from UsageFault INVSTATE with the stacked PC at Reset_Handler and stacked xPSR.T=0; the fault printer reports it.

scenarios.title: PendSV priority not lowest - the context switch runs inside an interrupt handler
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Under button presses, a long interrupt handler occasionally computes a wrong result and a task's counter jumps; with no button presses everything is fine.
scenarios.expected: With PendSV lowest, the button handler always finishes intact and every switch happens with EXC_RETURN 0xFFFFFFFD; with PendSV at 0x80, switches run on top of the handler (EXC_RETURN 0xFFFFFFF1) and the handler detects corrupted registers.

scenarios.title: SysTick period - off-by-one reload and a wrong clock assumption
scenarios.hidden_symptom: The scheduler tick looks right in the debugger, but task periods measured on the scope are 12.5 times too long (or drift slowly).
scenarios.expected: correct gives 150000 cycles and 1000 us per tick; off_by_one gives 150001 cycles per tick; wrong_clock gives 150000 cycles but 12500 us per tick.

scenarios.title: SVC returns the wrong value - result written to the live r0, not the stacked r0
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Output appears normally, but every system call reports failure to its caller.
scenarios.expected: No faults, the alphabet is printed, but every write() returns its argument instead of 1, so svc_errors climbs and task B reports it.

scenarios.title: Button interrupt does nothing - NVIC not enabled vs no handler installed
scenarios.hidden_symptom: Pressing the button does nothing. In one build the program keeps running normally; in another build it freezes on the first press.
scenarios.expected: not_enabled shows the IRQ pending but never taken (no exception entry, presses=0, the run ends on max_cycles); no_handler enters IRQ_GPIO at Default_Handler and stays there.
